 EDUCATION 
 Bob Ferguson continues to drag feet on federal education tax credit as deadline looms
 WA Gov. Bob Ferguson still hasn't decided if he is going to enroll his state into a federal education tax credit program with the deadline just two months away.
 BY JACKSON MEYER 
 Nov 4, 2026, 5:25 AM 
 0 
 Follow on Google News
 WA Governor Bob Ferguson still hasn't opted into a federal education tax credit program. (Office of Governor/Facebook)
 (Office of Governor/Facebook)
 The clock is ticking and Washington Governor Bob Ferguson still hasn’t opted into a federal education tax credit program that could save families thousands of dollars per year.
 The program was part of President Donald Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act. It gives any federal taxpayer a dollar-for-dollar credit of up to $1,700 for donating to an approved scholarship granting organization, which then distributes money to families for tuition, tutoring, books, technology and other education costs. States have to opt in before January 2027 for their students to benefit, and the decision sits with the governor. Ferguson still hasn’t made one, and he’s never really explained why.
 “I have not received any inquiries personally from either the governor or from the superintendent,” Education Secretary Linda McMahon told The Jason Rantz Show on Seattle Red 770 AM last month.
 Ferguson’s excuses
 Ferguson’s previous excuse was that he was waiting for the federal regulations to be released before opting in. However, those regulations were released in October and he still hasn’t made a decision.
 “The governor’s position has not changed,” spokesperson Brionna Aho said in an email last week. “He has made it clear we would review the rules thoroughly before making a decision. Now that we have the rules, that review is underway.”
 Opponents of the program argue that its just a backdoor way of implementing a private-school voucher system with very little state oversight. They also say there’s no guarantee the funds would benefit public school students because taxpayers decide which scholarship-granting organizations they want their donation to go to, including ones that would only fund private-school-related expenses.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 “I’m deeply skeptical of voucher programs that could harm our public school system,” Ferguson wrote in the Seattle Times earlier this year. “I’ve directed my team to analyze whether we can use these funds in a way that benefits public school students.”
 Critics say Ferguson gets the facts wrong
 Supporters counter that the money is privately donated, not appropriated, so the voucher label does not apply. The Washington Policy Center estimates the program could route more than $700 million a year to Washington students at no cost to state taxpayers, a figure that State Superintendent Chris Reykdal has publicly dismissed .
 “Bob Ferguson still refuses to give families thousands of dollars a year in tax relief for education costs,” State Rep. Travis Couture (R-Allyn) wrote on X back in August. “It costs our state absolutely nothing, yet for no reason he resists. That tracks with the governor cutting hundreds of millions from education every year he’s been in office. The governor cares more about radical special interests than students or families.”
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 Congressman Michael Baumgartner (R-WA) also encouraged Ferguson to do his job and opt in just as over 30 other states have, including many blue states.
 “Governor Ferguson has had plenty of time to take a look at this. I do believe that he’s being heavily influenced by the state superintendent, who literally has some incorrect facts in a letter that he has published stating why the governor should not opt in,” said McMahon. “This money does not take anything away from public education. It doesn’t come out of public funds. This is money that is donated by private donors.”
